KV also rejected and deleted: 1.27-1.46x end to end, needs a second 9.4GB weight to stay correct, +600-800 MiB on a card with ~340 MiB headroom. This card is now 'wire one 9B checkpoint' - materially smaller.

Dep half DONE, graph half BLOCKED. Four dep entries landed and verified: klein-9b-transformer (modelDeps), qwen3-8b-clip (assetDeps), klein-9b-lora-refcontrol-depth + klein-9b-lora-nsfw (loraDeps). Extends the brief: the qwen3-8b ENCODER filename lies the same way the transformer does - both are int8_tensorwise with a SCALAR weight_scale, while the shipped 4B weight is rowwise (weight_scale [3072,1]), so 4B and 9B are NOT the same quantisation despite near-identical names. BLOCKER: Input_is_9b exists in NO repo copy of the Klein graph. The bench template is a REDUCED LanPaint testbed (260 nodes vs the repo raw 338), and 92 of its 94 missing nodes are live - 64 of them ship in the runtime klein_t2i.json that Klein 4B runs today, including GrowMaskWithBlur and ImageCompositeMasked entirely, 6 of 11 CLIPTextEncode, 6 of 11 ReferenceLatent, 2 of 3 InpaintCrop/StitchImproved, a whole sampler stack and the entire Input_Negative chain. Syncing it as-is would break inpaint, detail and upscale on the SHIPPED 4B model. The is_9b gate has to be applied to the FULL 338-node template in ComfyUI, or 9B ships its own graph on a reduced op set - that is a product call, asked of Fabio 2026-08-22.

Klein 9B is wired. Fabio saved the consolidated template; sync-raw-workflows committed the raw source, converted to API, passed validate-injection-rules and baked BOTH runtimes. generate_klein.py now emits one runtime per SIZE from the single template - four weight names plus the Input_is_9b gate - so there is no 9B twin template to maintain and a graph edit lands on both sizes at once. Swap targets bind by class with exact-count asserts, never by node id. klein-9b ModelDef landed styleless (styleLoras false, styleOps empty, rack nodes still in the graph behind the gate), sharing modelFamily FLUX.2-Klein with 4B at a distinct sizeTier so the L/B badge disambiguates. LanPaint pinned upstream at scraed/LanPaint 9fe91955 (tag v2.1.0, GPL-3.0, not forked - bench copy verified byte-identical to that commit first) and declared on BOTH sizes. CORRECTION to this session earlier: the claim that syncing the template would break shipped 4B was WRONG. It measured node-ID identity across a restructure. R2 upload COMPLETE and verified - all four Klein 9B weights (18.02 GB) return HTTP 200 at their public models.cubric.studio URLs with byte counts matching their dep entries exactly. Ran serialized at the 3M cap, 2.98 MB/s throughout. Offline resolver verification also clean: all seven ops resolve to klein_9b_t2i.json (on disk), 13 deps resolve with zero 4B leakage, and all seven 4B ops still resolve to klein_t2i.json unchanged. Two apparent failures in that pass were BAD ASSERTIONS, not defects, and are recorded so nobody re-chases them: selectableOps returns [] for EVERY model in the fleet (hasOperationGroups is false since the operations{} shape was removed 2026-08-07, and the function short-circuits on it), and resolveWorkflowFile appends _stage2 for klein-4b identically to klein-9b - inherited resolver behaviour guarded upstream by multiStage:false, which 4B has shipped with. Also note resolveDeps depExists is a REGISTRY validator (id => !!DEPS[id]), not an install check; passing () => false makes it throw correctly. Still open: the Pod smoke (Fabio wants to be present, so it waits to be asked), klein-9b.webp, and the two doc/convention follow-ups.

KLEIN 9B PROVEN IN THE REAL APP. Fabio restarted his instance and ran a t2i; the sidecar records model: klein-9b, operation: t2i, 896x1088, prompt "A woman walking a tiger on a beach". That one run exercised the whole chain this card wired - the ModelDef, the MPI-357 licence gate going live for the first time, dep resolution against G:/CubricModels via the engine extra_model_paths base_path, the LanPaint install into the app engine from the pinned commit, and the generated klein_9b_t2i.json. Local-first was Fabio's call and it was the right order: it proved the wiring before any Pod spend AND produced the display asset. klein-9b.webp placed - converted from the source PNG at native 896x1088 (the fleet convention, matching klein-4b and krea2), webp q85, 95,878 bytes against klein-4b's 83,216. Encoded from the PNG, never from an encoded buffer. Every ModelDef image in the fleet now resolves on disk; npm test still 680 pass 0 fail. NOT yet exercised: the other six ops (i2i, control, kleinEdit, inpaint, detail, upscale). They share the one graph but take different wf_type branches, so the Pod smoke is what covers them. Smoke still waiting on Fabio (he wants to be present) AND on the evidence-file choice - smoke-evidence.json is stale since 846dc777 (2026-08-17, MPI-325), so a --models subset cannot merge into it.

UNRELEASED.md carries the Klein 9B story in full now. Two bullets changed and one is new. The two-sizes bullet's closing line 'Style LoRAs are 4B-only for now' was false the moment the styles agent shipped - replaced with 'Each size brings its own styles'. NEW bullet names all seven 9B styles (Storybook, Comic, Anime, Chibi, Doodle, Vintage, Watercolour) and, per the agent's explicit request, does NOT present them as 4B's styles moved across: only Anime/Chibi/Doodle are the same artists' 9B builds, the rest are different artists' weights, which is why the labels differ - Storybook is mid-century storybook illustration not Fluxtoon, Comic is pulp not manga, 9B's Vintage is 1960s-80s where 4B's is 1920s. Muppets and Jojo have no 9B weight in existence, so seven reads as a fact rather than a shortfall. Chibi's overfit is folded in as a Stylization hint. The INPAINT bullet also gained the MPI-367 truth: the model sees under the mask, and an empty prompt no longer erases. GATE 0 RUN PER BULLET against v1.4.2, not assumed - it ships InpaintStitchImproved x3 with zero LanPaint, node 367 is literally MpiString {string: 'Remove'} (the injected word), and 4B's eight styles are at models.js:933. So every 'used to' claim describes released behaviour rather than churn inside this unreleased cycle. Agent's report verified independently before use: four commits resolve, labels match, seven dep entries present, eight picker webps on disk, Input_is_9b gone.
